note: MOD_PLAN A30 (Fiddler, token-count threshold for the CPU share in prefill). The preset arms the CPU share (STRATA_PREFILL_CPU_SHARE 0.6) for every chunk below STRATA_PREFILL_CPU_SHARE_MAX 4096 tokens: the decode CPU pool computes part of the experts while the GPU streams the rest. Agent turns are deltas of ~1-3K tokens, the window where the row estimates up to ~0.4 s per turn. share0 = share off (the GPU takes every expert), max1024 / max2048 = the share only below 1024 / 2048 tokens (a 3K delta then skips it), base = share up to 4096. long1k / long3k are cold 1000 / 3000-token prompts (abtest cases added for this; metric = prompt tok/s of the engine's own log line, one request per server, placed after a 'short' warm-up so the first request does not pay the cold start); edit (~2K tokens of C++) also records its prompt tok/s in the jsonl rows. Lossy: the staged CPU experts differ from the GPU path by rounding (mean KL ~0.004 below 1024 tokens, ~0.011 at 1-3K, per the engine's own start-up note), so a faster arm that changes the text needs the token-forcing gate; an arm that is not faster than base is dropped. Decide on long3k (and long1k): promote only an arm with >= +2% prompt tok/s and no case below -3% (screen thresholds); short is the decode sanity case (the share does not touch decode). Source check 2026-11-11 (pancake-docs/batch3/agentloop.md): Fiddler's rule is per EXPERT (CPU when the CPU latency for the s tokens routed to that expert is below the GPU latency plus the weight copy; CPU latency linear in s, the copy constant), not per chunk, and the engine already has it: only non-resident experts with at most MAXT (8) tokens go to the CPU, fewest tokens first, STRATA_PREFILL_CPU_SHARE of the streamed ones. q2_rows_bench on the 5700G (one thread, legacy kernel) gives ~220 us per expert and token and x2.4 for 4 tokens, so with the 42 us pool time at s = 1 the CPU takes ~21.7 + 20.6 s us against a 115 us promotion: break-even s ~ 4.5 tokens (MAXT 8 is above it; harmless while the CPU and the link work at the same time). Arm auto = the measured break-even (the engine measures the CPU and GPU cost per expert and gates itself); the chunk limits max1024 / max2048 only decide whether a chunk is staged at all.
